judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Reading Skills (coordinate rank 0, Grade R) addressing beginning sounds in names. The first sits in Term 2 under sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words' and asks the learner to recognise sounds at the beginning of some words such as friends' names. The second sits in Term 4 under 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness' and extends this to the generalised insight that words are made up of sounds, exemplified by the beginning letter/s of their names, adding an explicit sound-letter link and a structural understanding of words rather than isolated beginning-sound recognition. This is substantive deepening, not mere repeated wording, and the earlier-term perceptual skill plausibly supports success in the later-term conceptual/letter-linked statement; direction Term 2 to Term 4 respects the within-grade term order. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, identity scopes and LC tags.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Writing handwriting Skills (rank 0, Grade R). The first sits under Term 1 / Emergent Handwriting ('Traces simple outlines of pictures and patterns'); the second sits under Term 2 / Handwriting ('Copies patterns onto pegboards and copies patterns, words and letters onto paper'). This is an earlier-to-same-or-later Term direction within one grade, and the change is substantive rather than mere repetition: tracing over a given outline is a supported, guided fine-motor pattern activity, whereas Term 2 requires reproducing patterns independently in a different medium (pegboards) and extends the content from pictures/patterns to words and letters on paper. Control gained in tracing patterns plausibly supports success in copying patterns, words and letters, so a Term 1 to Term 2 buildsTowards is justified. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the printed statement text, identity scopes and Term ancestry supplied are unambiguous.

The first covers morphological word parts (recognising and using prefixes un-, re- and suffixes -ful, -ness); the second covers phonological segmentation of multi-syllabic words into syllables (re-mem-ber). These are complementary word-analysis strategies for tackling longer words, reinforcing each other, but neither statement's text or LCs (tags: phonics/prefixes/suffixes vs phonics/syllables/segmenting) shows that proficiency in one is substantively required for or expands into the other. With identical Grade rank (3) and identical Term (4), there is no substantive evidence for a developmental direction, so the symmetric relation is appropriate; the shared token 're' is incidental (prefix vs syllable example). Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the available statement text is sufficient for this coherence judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0), so direction rests on within-grade Term order from the source identity scopes. The second SFI is Grade R / Term 2 / Emergent Reading / 'Emergent reading skills': 'Develops directionality such as moving blocks from left to right and top to bottom' - a concrete, manipulative introduction to the left-to-right, top-to-bottom orientation (source context row shows it paired with eye-movement tracking). The first SFI is Grade R / Term 4 / Emergent Writing / 'Emergent Writing': "'Writes' observing conventions of directionality: 'writes' from left to right, top to bottom of page" - the same directional convention now applied independently to mark-making on a page. This is substantive extension rather than generic repetition: the later statement moves from manipulating objects to governing the learner's own emergent writing across a page, and secure grasp of the orientation developed in Term 2 plausibly supports success with the Term 4 writing convention. Direction second_to_first keeps the permitted earlier-Term-to-later-Term order within Grade R. Shared LC tags (directionality, left to right, top to bottom) corroborate but are not the sole basis; note both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text and identity scopes shown.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade R (rank 0) Skills. The second SFI sits in Grade R Term 1 under Emergent Reading / 'Emergent reading skills' and states 'Uses memory skills to recall items seen such as letters, shapes or concrete objects' (LC tags: emergent reading, memory, recall, visual memory). The first SFI sits in Grade R Term 2 under Listening and Speaking (Oral) / 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning' and states 'Distinguishes between the shape of different letters and words. For example, sorts identical objects, views a sequence of nearly identical pictures and picks out the one that is different and explains why it is different' (LC tags: letter shapes, sorting, visual discrimination, word shapes). These are distinct, complementary emergent-literacy visual capabilities - recall of seen items versus discrimination, sorting and justification of differences - operating on the same concrete objects of attention (letters, shapes, objects). The Term 2 statement is not a deepening, broadening or more-complex form of the Term 1 memory statement, so the substantive-extension bar for buildsTowards is not met; the nomination signals are weak and non-semantic (shared Grade ancestor at distance 4, rank gap 0, LC tag Jaccard 0.10 on 'visual', text token Jaccard 0.05 on 'letters'/'objects', trigram overlap driven by those same words). The pair nevertheless shows meaningful pair-specific coherence and mutual reinforcement within Grade R emergent visual-perceptual literacy work, which exceeds generic repetition and supports symmetric relatesTo with null direction and unchanged canonical endpoint order. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this remains an inferred curriculum-grounded relation, not an empirical prerequisite claim.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 3 (rank 3), Reading and Phonics, Sub-strand 'Group Guided Reading': the first is Term 3 ('Uses a range of self-correcting methods when reading: re-reading, reading on, pausing') and the second is Term 4 ('Uses self-correcting strategies when reading: reading, pausing, practising a word before saying it aloud'). They address the same guided-reading self-monitoring and self-correction capability with a varied list of strategies, so they are substantively coherent and mutually reinforcing across consecutive terms. They are not, however, a justified developmental step: the stem is near-identical, each lists three strategies, Term 4 substitutes 'practising a word before saying it aloud' while dropping 're-reading' and 'reading on', and Term 4 narrows 'a range of self-correcting methods' to 'self-correcting strategies'. There is no evidence of longer or more complex texts, greater independence, or broader repertoire, so the high token/trigram and LC-tag overlap plus adjacent-term placement cannot support buildsTowards in this deliberately repetitive CAPS framework. This is more than generic repetition (same sub-strand, continued explicit self-correction instruction), so canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the correct complete judgment; canonical endpoint order is preserved and is not semantic. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1, Term 2, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics' (ranks identical, Grade 1), but under different printed sub-strands: 'Reads phonic words in sentences and other texts' under the daily Phonics activities, and 'Discusses the use of capital letters and full stops' under Shared Reading. They are complementary sentence-level print skills — decoding taught phonic words within connected text, and attending to the sentence-boundary conventions (capitals, full stops) encountered when reading that same connected text — so they reinforce one another in Term 2 reading instruction. Neither statement's evidence shows that proficiency in one supports success in the other: decoding does not require punctuation discussion, and punctuation talk during shared reading is teacher-mediated and not dependent on independent phonic decoding. Token/trigram overlap is negligible ('and', 'the'), and shared ancestry, same page (67) and same table row are placement facts only, so no developmental direction is asserted; a same-grade, same-term symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so the full statement context is only partially visible.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R, Term 3, Emergent Reading / 'Emergent reading skills' Skill bullets from the same printed table row: 'Pretends to "read" and adopts a "reading" voice' and 'Discusses book handling and care'. They are complementary emergent-reading-with-books behaviours (pretend reading with expressive voice; talking about how to handle and care for books), sharing the LC tag cluster around books/emergent reading, but neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: pretend reading is a role-play/expression behaviour, while book handling and care is a print-concept/stewardship discussion. Same grade rank (Grade R, rank 0) and same Term 3, so no term-based developmental direction is available, and no substantive evidence of deepening or extension exists in either direction. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Listening and Speaking (Oral), under the identically worded Sub-strand 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning', but in different terms: the second SFI is Term 1 ('Participates in activities to perceive objects in the foreground and the background and to separate them meaningfully such as finds an image in a busy or detailed picture'; LCs 'Perceives objects in the foreground and the background' and 'Separates objects in the foreground and background meaningfully') and the first SFI is Term 3 ('Finds object hidden in a classroom among other items and guides peers to items using simple directions'; LCs 'Finds an object hidden in a classroom among other items' and 'Guides peers to items using simple directions'). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 1 statement establishes figure-ground visual discrimination within pictures, and the Term 3 statement transfers that discrimination to locating a real object embedded among distractors in the classroom and adds an oral production demand (giving simple positional directions to peers). Within-grade direction therefore runs from the earlier Term 1 skill to the later, extended Term 3 skill, which is the permitted second_to_first orientation under the canonical endpoint order. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.
